country.it.name: Italy
country.it.title: reimbursement by the national health service
country.it.lede: AIFA negotiates price and reimbursement with the company, and access starts when the decision is published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale. Until then a new drug can usually be sold only in class C(nn), which the national health service does not pay for.
country.it.mix_sub: Class of the first reimbursement decision (H: hospital use; A: community pharmacies), and drugs not yet reimbursed when checked.
country.it.note: Regional formulary listing can add months after the national decision and is not measured; early access under Law 648/96 or the AIFA 5% fund is not counted.
country.de.name: Germany
country.de.title: the G-BA benefit assessment
country.de.lede: In Germany a new drug is reimbursed from launch. Within about six months the G-BA decides its added benefit over an appropriate comparator (AMNOG), and that verdict is the basis for the price the company then negotiates with the statutory health insurers.
country.de.mix_sub: Each drug's best rating in its first concluded assessment.
country.de.note: For orphan drugs below the revenue threshold, added benefit is deemed proven by law; reserve antibiotics get no quantified rating and are left blank.
country.fr.name: France
country.fr.title: the HAS opinion on reimbursement
country.fr.lede: The HAS Transparency Committee rates whether a drug merits reimbursement at all (SMR) and its added benefit over existing care (ASMR I to V). The opinion opens price negotiations with the CEPS; the listing that gives patients access usually follows months later.
country.fr.mix_sub: Best ASMR across the opinion's indications, or SMR insufficient (judged not worth reimbursing).
country.fr.note: The milestone is the HAS opinion, not the later price and listing decision; drugs with no HAS opinion when checked count as waiting.
country.en.name: England
country.en.title: NICE guidance
country.en.lede: NICE appraises whether a drug is good value for the NHS at the price offered. A positive recommendation obliges the NHS in England to fund it, normally within three months.
country.en.mix_sub: Outcome of the first published appraisal for the drug's first indication.
country.en.note: England uses its own UK licence since Brexit, but times are counted from EC approval for comparability; drugs NICE will not appraise stay in the count as waiting.
